subtitle: How a wandering ascetic and a republican chief tied a clan’s hall to an unseen path

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of a wooden assembly hall above the Ganga plain at dusk
panels.action: Vardhamana Mahavira stands serene at the edge of a great republican hall in Vaishali while Chetaka, cloaked in authority, looks out over a gathering of clan chiefs beneath a sky streaked with fading light.

dialogue.text: In the age of the mahajanapadas, one quiet wanderer and one wary clan-chief turned a village birth into a republic’s argument: Mahavira in the house of the Naya chiefs.

i18n.hi: महाजनपदों के युग में, एक शांत यात्री और एक सतर्क कुलप्रमुख ने जन्म को बना दिया गणराज की बहस: नाया सरदारों के घर महावीर।

panels.shot: broad aerial vista over the north Bihar plains with rivers and clustered settlements
panels.action: The camera glides over a patchwork of fields and groves, dotted with mud-walled villages and a few fortified towns strung along the shining ribbon of the Ganga.

dialogue.text: Before empires, this land was a quilt of republics and kingdoms. In the north, the Vajji clans held their councils beneath open skies.

i18n.hi: साम्राज्यों से पहले, यह धरती गणों–राज्यों की रजाई थी। उत्तर में वज्जी कुल खुले आसमान तले सभा लगाते थे।

panels.shot: medium wide of Kundagrama near Vaishali with a modest kshatriya household
panels.action: Young Vardhamana, still in simple princely dress, walks through the courtyard of a modest but orderly kshatriya compound in a village grove, elders watching with quiet pride.

dialogue.text: Jain tradition places Vardhamana in Kundagrama, a Naya or Jnatrika kshatriya settlement near Vaishali, born into a clan that shared blood with the Licchavis.

i18n.hi: जैन परंपरा वर्धमान को कुंडग्राम में रखती है, वैशाली के पास नाया/ज्ञात्रिक क्षत्रिय बसाहट, जो लिच्छवियों के खून से जुड़ी थी।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot of a household gathering with women and a dignified elder
panels.action: Trisala, dignified and composed, sits with other women as a messenger bows before an older Chetaka, who is visiting the household, his presence bringing a subtle shift in deference.

dialogue.text: His mother, Trisala, is remembered as a sister of Chetaka, the powerful Licchavi chief of Vaishali. Through her, the boy’s courtyard opened into a republic’s hall.

i18n.hi: उसकी माँ त्रिशला, वैशाली के शक्तिशाली लिच्छवि नायक चेटक की बहन मानी जाती है। उसके सहारे लड़के का आँगन खुला एक गणसभा में।

panels.shot: low-angle inside the gana-sabha hall, wooden pillars and benches filled with chiefs
panels.action: Chetaka presides at the center of a broad wooden hall, flanked by seated clan representatives, their faces intent as they listen to a heated but ordered debate.

dialogue.text: The Licchavis and their allies called their chiefs to a gana-sabha. Decisions rose not from a throne, but from benches of equals where voices weighed more than crowns.

i18n.hi: लिच्छवि और उनके साथी अपने सरदारों को गणसभा में बुलाते थे। फैसले तख्त से नहीं, बराबरी की पंक्ति से उठते, जहाँ आवाजें ताज से भारी थीं।

panels.shot: close-up on young Vardhamana at the edge of the hall, half in shadow
panels.action: Vardhamana stands quietly in the shadows of the hall entrance, watching Chetaka argue a point with calm force, the murmur of the assembly a soft blur around him.

dialogue.text: In such halls the young Naya would see power as a thing argued and shared. Later, Jain texts would remember him not as a prince of one court, but as kin to many councils.

i18n.hi: ऐसी सभाओं में नाया बालक ने देखा कि ताकत बहस और बाँटने की चीज है। बाद के जैन ग्रंथ उसे एक दरबार का राजकुमार नहीं, कई सभाओं का अपना मानेंगे।

panels.shot: medium shot of a domestic scene with elders discussing marriage alliances over a map-like cloth
panels.action: Chetaka leans over a simple cloth map marked with rivers and towns as messengers kneel, while Trisala listens, a thoughtful Vardhamana in the background; small tokens mark distant cities.

dialogue.text: Later Jain accounts speak of Chetaka’s many daughters married into Vatsa, Anga, Avanti and other courts, tying the Licchavi house to far-off capitals by marriage and obligation.

i18n.hi: बाद की कथाएँ कहती हैं, चेटक की बेटियाँ वत्स, अंग, अवंती और दूसरे दरबारों में ब्याही गईं, लिच्छवि घर को दूर-दूर की राजधानियों से रिश्ते और कर्ज में बाँधते हुए।

panels.shot: montage-like wide shot showing palanquins leaving Vaishali towards different horizons
panels.action: Several palanquins, each with a veiled bride, depart Vaishali’s gate in different directions, escorted by small retinues; Chetaka watches from the rampart, arms folded, expression unreadable.

dialogue.text: Through such alliances, a republican chief stitched a web of kinship across the Ganga valley. Along those paths, gifts, news—and new teachings—would later travel.

i18n.hi: ऐसे समझौतों से एक गणप्रमुख ने गंगा घाटी में रिश्तों का जाल सी दिया। इन्हीं राहों से फिर उपहार, खबरें—and नई शिक्षाएँ चल पड़ीं।

panels.shot: quiet interior night shot of Vardhamana seated in contemplation as family sleeps
panels.action: By lamplight, Vardhamana sits cross-legged in a bare corner, eyes lowered in deep thought, while his family sleeps behind a curtain; an unseen breeze stirs the flame.

dialogue.text: Yet the Naya youth’s thoughts moved beyond clan and council. The Acaranga and Bhagavati sutras remember years of inner restlessness before he left the house of his kin.

i18n.hi: पर नाया युवक के खयाल कुल और सभा से आगे बहने लगे। आचारांग और भगवती सूत्र घर छोड़ने से पहले की बरसों की भीतर की बैचेनी याद रखते हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot at the village edge as Vardhamana prepares to depart, family and Chetaka nearby
panels.action: At the edge of Kundagrama, Vardhamana, now simply robed, stands with a staff; Trisala’s face is tense, while Chetaka, older and grave, rests a hand briefly on the young man’s shoulder.

dialogue.speaker: vardhamana_mahavira_and_chetaka
dialogue.text: Kinship binds bodies, Chetaka. I seek a binding that harms none.

i18n.hi: रिश्ता शरीरों को बाँधता है, चेटक। मैं वह बंधन खोज रहा हूँ जो किसी को चोट न दे।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of Chetaka watching Vardhamana’s receding figure on a dusty road
panels.action: Chetaka stands on a small rise, his figure strong but still, as Vardhamana’s lone figure walks away down a dusty path lined with trees.

dialogue.text: The Kalpa Sutra will celebrate this renunciation in sacred tones. Modern historians remind us these are layered memories, not court records, but they agree on the path: from kshatriya house to homeless wandering.

i18n.hi: कल्पसूत्र इस त्याग को पवित्र स्वर में गाएगा। आधुनिक इतिहासकार कहेंगे, ये परतदार स्मृतियाँ हैं, राज-दस्तावेज नहीं; लेकिन एक रेखा पर सब मानते हैं: क्षत्रिय घर से बेघर संन्यास तक।

panels.shot: wide shot of Mahavira as ascetic begging in a market town watched by curious townsfolk
panels.action: Years later, Vardhamana, now Mahavira, stands thin and composed in the street of a bustling town, accepting alms in a cupped hand while merchants and villagers watch, some respectful, some skeptical.

dialogue.text: The texts show him moving through Magadha and Kosala, practicing severe restraint, teaching by presence more than word. His path crossed many towns that knew Licchavi and Naya names.

i18n.hi: ग्रंथ उसे मगध और कोशल में घूमते दिखाते हैं, कड़ी तपस्या करते, शब्द से ज्यादा उपस्थिति से सिखाते। उसका मार्ग कई नगरों से गुज़रा जो लिच्छवि और नाया नामों से परिचित थे।

panels.shot: interior of Vaishali hall again, this time with an ascetic seated before Chetaka
panels.action: Inside the gana-sabha hall, Mahavira, now shaven-headed and austere, sits on a simple mat facing Chetaka and other chiefs, who lean forward, listening to the ascetic’s quiet, firm presence.

dialogue.text: Jain tradition keeps Mahavira close to Vaishali. It remembers Chetaka as a supporter, his house a refuge where the ascetic’s teachings could be heard without royal fear.

i18n.hi: जैन परंपरा महावीर को वैशाली से ही जोड़े रखती है। वह चेटक को सहायक मानती है, उसका घर ऐसा आसरा जहाँ तपस्वी की आवाज़ राजभय के बिना सुनी जा सके।

panels.shot: tight two-shot on Mahavira and Chetaka in a private verandah after the assembly
panels.action: On a quiet verandah overlooking trees, Chetaka sits with his back to a pillar, while Mahavira faces him, legs folded, their eyes meeting in a rare, candid moment away from the crowd.

dialogue.speaker: vardhamana_mahavira_and_chetaka
dialogue.text: We argue laws, Vardhamana. Can your vows live in such noisy halls?

i18n.hi: हम क़ानून पर बहस करते हैं, वर्धमान। तुम्हारी प्रतिज्ञाएँ ऐसी शोरभरी सभा में टिक पाएँगी?

panels.shot: close-up on Mahavira’s calm face, soft background blur of the hall
panels.action: Mahavira’s face is steady, lit by soft light from the side; behind him, the blurred shape of the hall and faint silhouettes of debating chiefs suggest the world he has stepped beyond yet still influences.

dialogue.speaker: vardhamana_mahavira_and_chetaka
dialogue.text: The hall is loud, Chetaka. But each mind is a quiet place where vows begin.

i18n.hi: सभा शोर से भरी है, चेटक। पर हर मन एक शांत जगह है, जहाँ प्रतिज्ञा जन्म लेती है।

panels.shot: wide shot of messengers departing Vaishali toward various courts with scrolls and gifts
panels.action: Mounted envoys and foot-messengers leave Vaishali’s gate carrying bundles and small chests, one pausing to bow to Mahavira as he stands aside, while Chetaka watches from the walls.

dialogue.text: Later Jain authors would see Jain lay communities growing in cities linked to Chetaka’s alliances. They imagined teachings carried along the same roads as brides and letters.

i18n.hi: बाद के जैन लेखक जैन श्रावक–समुदायों को उन्हीं नगरों में उगता देखते हैं जो चेटक की सड़कों से जुड़े थे। वे मानते हैं, जहाँ दुल्हनें और खत चलते थे, वहीं उपदेश भी चले।

panels.shot: documentary-style overlay shot of texts being copied in a later monastic library
panels.action: Centuries later, monks in a quiet library copy palm-leaf manuscripts by lamplight; one leaf bears the words of the Kalpa Sutra, while images of Mahavira and Chetaka fade ghostlike above them.

dialogue.text: The Kalpa Sutra and allied texts fixed this memory: Mahavira as Naya-born, kin to Licchavis. Modern scholars trace in it the map of republican politics beneath the sacred story.

i18n.hi: कल्पसूत्र और उसके साथी ग्रंथों ने यह स्मृति गाड़ दी: महावीर नाया जन्म, लिच्छवियों के सगे। आधुनिक विद्वान इस कथा में गणराजनीति का नक्शा पढ़ते हैं, जो पवित्र कथा के नीचे छुपा है।

panels.shot: final contemplative wide shot of the empty Vaishali hall at dawn, with distant ascetic silhouette
panels.action: At dawn, the Vaishali assembly hall stands empty, golden light slanting between pillars; far beyond, a lone ascetic silhouette walks along a tree-lined ridge, the river mist rising below.

dialogue.text: In the house of the Naya chiefs, we see how ideas moved: through kinship, roads and argument, a silent ascetic and a talking chief binding a restless republic to an unseen, inner law.

i18n.hi: नाया सरदारों के घर हम देखते हैं, सोच कैसे चली: रिश्तों, सड़कों और बहसों से—एक मौन तपस्वी और एक बोलता सरदार, जो बेचैन गणराज को एक अदृश्य, भीतरी नियम से बाँध रहे थे।

title_i18n.en: Mahavira in the House of the Naya Chiefs

subtitle_i18n.en: How a wandering ascetic and a republican chief tied a clan’s hall to an unseen path
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे एक घूमता तपस्वी और एक गणप्रमुख ने कुल की सभा को अदृश्य राह से बाँधा
